guides.favoredWhen: Respect his faster hook and ult windows; poke him down early and keep your roams short.

keyTips.text: His hook travels faster than yours, so never hook first into him: he can answer yours on reaction and turn it around.
He has real kill pressure on your carry, so keep your roams short and return before he punishes your absence.
Poke him out at level 1 from behind your wave, so he cannot take his level-2 all-in at full strength.

tips.text: Contest level 1 with autos and spells through the wave: every bit of health he loses weakens his level-2 spike.
Never get hooked while the wave crashes into you: hooked under your own tower is the one place his engage kills.
Track his ult ({cd:111:R}) and give ground while it is up; take the fight only after he has spent it.
Rotate behind terrain instead of through open river: walls break his hook angles, and he hooks whatever walks into his lane.
Force out his ult without committing, then turn and zone him while it is down for its full cooldown.
When he hooks your carry, answer with the lantern shield instead of engaging back: surviving his window wins you the fight.

guides.favoredWhen: Punish his spent shield and decide the lane through your carry instead of hook fishing.

keyTips.text: Punish him when he spends his shield on trades: without it he cannot stand in front of his carry.
A first-hook kill attempt is a valid early call: go when the wave and your carry let you collapse on him.
Read the duo at load-in, not just him: hard-engage carries with Braum out-threaten poke duos, and that decides whether the lane stays quiet or turns bloody.

tips.text: Look for the early hook kill before his defensive line settles: do not wait for a perfect later angle that never comes.
Trade into him while his shield is down ({cd:201:E}): that is when your autos and spells actually stick.
When your carries are ahead, play for lantern over forcing hooks: repositioning them wins more than fishing for catches.
Ward only where the wave lets you defend the ward: a dead ward is worse than a late one.
Stop frontlining for hooks once fights start: peel with lantern and Flay so your carry plays the fight instead of watching you fish.
If their carry outscales yours, force the bloody version of the lane early: quiet even lanes favor Braum's wall.

guides.favoredWhen: Punish missed bubbles while she has no early heal, but never overcommit into her slows.

keyTips.text: She has no early heal, so hook her and lantern out: start the fight with Q and leave with W before she can turn it.
Punish a missed bubble, but do not overcommit: her slows let her carry chase you down after a long chase.
Check summoners at load-in: if she skipped Heal, every landed hook is a kill angle because she has no save for herself.

tips.text: Force plays early while she has no heal and no Mikael's: this window before her first sustain item is the strongest part of your lane.
Throw the hook the moment her bubble misses ({cd:267:Q}): patient hooks land, while forced attempts feed straight into her disengage.
Set dragon vision on your item timing, and only place wards where the wave lets you defend them.
Once she completes Mikael's, full hook combos stop working on her carry: switch to picks elsewhere instead of repeating the same play.
Kill Nami first in fights: without her, the enemy duo loses both its sustain and its disengage.
End the lane phase ahead: once her duo finishes its first items and levels, her peel outscales your pick potential.

keyTips.text: Thresh is strong early but has no sustain: skip the long-range poke lane when you cannot reach the brush or create an opening, and only fight with a real path in.
Aim hooks at the opponent's likely dodge direction, tracking whether the ADC or the support tends to evade left or right before throwing.
Create picks from fog with Death Sentence, then lantern an ally into the play or carry one out of danger, keeping Flay ready to peel or interrupt the next dash.

tips.text: After pushing a wave into the enemy tower, choose between a reset, a plate attempt, poke or a possible dive, or a roam; when roaming, never leave the ADC exposed.
A crashed wave opens a brief roam window before the next wave is likely to reach your tower; return before it dies if the ADC has not pushed it back out.
Leave plate gold for the ADC when safe, and threaten poke or a dive with the hook while the opponent sits under tower.
Against Cleanse, hold Ignite until after the opponent uses it on Death Sentence so both effects are not removed together.
Place the lantern in the direction the teammate is already moving to make it easier to click, repositioning allies for follow-up or peel.
Use the lantern to check a bush or cross a wall instead of face-checking, but keep it available when a gank may be coming.
Remember the lantern has unit collision: it can obstruct an enemy's path but can also accidentally block teammates, so place it deliberately.
Save Flay to peel or interrupt a dash, and against an opponent who escapes right as the hook ends, hold Flay for that exact moment.
Land Death Sentence, place The Box during its crowd control, and push the target into a wall with Flay for the stronger slow.

Ward while moving through fog and before objectives, adapting depth to enemy jungle mobility and the changed terrain around the third dragon and Baron; practice placements in Practice Tool until each ward lands repeatably.
Convert a pushed bot wave into a safe reset, tower pressure, a dive threat, or a short roam, always returning in time to protect the ADC's experience.
In teamfights, flex between engage and disengage: follow a pick with The Box, but preserve lantern and Flay when a teammate needs protection.

itemization.text: Follow the patch 26.21 default of Ionian Boots of Lucidity, Solstice Sleigh, Locket of the Iron Solari, Knight's Vow, Redemption, and Bandlepipes, favoring Locket as the broadly useful first core.

Take Knight's Vow for single-target damage, Redemption for slower front-to-back fights, and Bandlepipes with several auto attackers; choose Second Wind into poke, Bone Plating into early trading, Unflinching into trade-pattern crowd control, Aftershock into engage lanes or solo-frontline games, and Glacial Augment into double-ranged or dive-heavy opponents.
Round out defenses by threat: Frozen Heart against auto-attack damage, Thornmail for grievous wounds, Abyssal Mask with AP teammates, and Kaenic Rookern for more magic resistance.
